entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5657"/><title type="x-s2">PSALM 20</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ps.20.1-Ps.20.9">Psa 20:1-9</reference>. David probably composed this Psalm to express the prayers of the pious for his success as at once the head of the Church and nation. Like other compositions of which David in such relations is the subject, its sentiments have a permanent value--the prosperity of Christ's kingdom being involved, as well as typified, in that of Israel and its king.</title> <div sID="gen8603" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5657"/><hi type="bold">1. hear thee--</hi>graciously (<reference osisRef="Ps.4.1">Psa 4:1</reference>).<div eID="gen8603" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8604" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">name of--</hi>or manifested perfections, as power, wisdom, &c.<div eID="gen8604" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8605" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">defend thee--</hi>set thee on high from danger (<reference osisRef="Ps.9.9">Psa 9:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.18.3">18:3</reference>). <div eID="gen8605" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: PSALM 20 Psa 20:1-9 . David probably composed this Psalm to express the prayers of the pious for his success as at once the head of the Church and nation. Like other compositions of which David in such relations is the subject, its sentiments have a permanent value--the prosperity of Christ's kingdom being involved, as well as typified, in that of Israel and its king. 1. hear thee-- graciously ( Psa 4:1 ). name of-- or manifested perfections, as power, wisdom, &c. defend thee-- set thee on high from danger ( Psa 9:9 ; 18:3 ).
